newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend slide on profit-taking, data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend slide on profit-taking, data.

text.p: Mexico stocks fell Wednesday after weak industrial output figures spurred a renewed bout of profit-taking.

"This is basically normal and even healthy profit-taking, which doesn't change the outlook for the bourse reaching all-time highs and closing May at 4,000 points," said Diego Candano, research director at the Ixe brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 36.54 points, or 0.93 percent, at 3,894.20.
Candano said weaker-than-expected industrial activity data released in late trade also caused stocks to close lower.

"The industrial output data did impact the market. The figures were not so bad themselves, they were just lower than expectations. You have to take into account that Easter came early this year," he said.

Mexico's industrial production increased by 4.2 percent in year-on-year terms in March. This compares with an average increase of 7.65 percent predicted in a Reuters survey of 10 financial firms in Mexico City.
The market also was hit by a statement by Marxist guerrillas that their forces clashed recently with the Mexican army and they predicted more fighting as the government steps up efforts to hunt them.
The Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Wednesday that their forces had clashed with the army, causing casualties on both sides, but gave no specific dates.
"The EPR business is making waves, so whatever is going on, it's best to take profits," a floor trader said.

Telmex contributed most to the slide and accounted for 22 percent of all shares traded. The telecomms firm's L shares ended down eight centavos (1 cent) at 17.16 pesos ($2.17), while its ADRs closed off 3/8 to 43-1/8 on Wall Street.
Trading volume was brisk at 102.6 million shares.
On the broad market, 105 stocks were traded, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 59 to 29.
Shares listed by the troubled Sidek conglomerate and its Situr tourist subsidiary headed the prominent gainers' list for the third session in a row.

Sidek A class, or preferred shares gained six centavos (less than 1 cent) to 42 centavos (5 cents), while Situr B class, or common shares gained three centavos (less than 1 cent) to 51 centavos (6 cents).

"There are rumours of a forthcoming debt restructuring deal, and they're buying on them. The interesting thing is the increase in volume. The only one in the group that is quiet is Simec," a promotor at a brokerage said.
